title: French students block streets in protests over grievances and policy culture
content:
France is witnessing a wave of school protests, with students organizing blockades and marches across the country.  

According to reports, the demonstrations stem from genuine grievances among students and reflect France’s longstanding practice of addressing policy issues through street actions.

title: Margaret Hamilton, Apollo 11 software lead, dies at 90
content:
Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering computer scientist whose software helped land Apollo 11 on the Moon, died at age 90.  

Hamilton led the development of the software for NASA’s Apollo mission and was later awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom for her contributions.  

Her work was instrumental to the success of the Apollo program.
summary: Margaret Hamilton, a pioneering computer scientist who led the development of software that helped land Apollo 11 on the Moon, died at age 90. She was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

title: Tuchel names England squad with only 12 World Cup players available for Nations League
content:
England manager Thomas Tuchel initially intended to prioritize continuity by retaining the majority of the squad that reached the World Cup semi-finals in North America. However, a series of injuries forced significant changes to his plans for the four-match Nations League window. By the time of the final match against Czechia at Wembley, only 12 players from the original World Cup group remained available to Tuchel.

The squad selection has produced distinct outcomes for individual players. Alex Scott, Lewis Hall, and Myles Lewis-Skelly are described as clear winners who are moving forward, while others have been left behind due to the rapid turnover of personnel. Tuchel acknowledged that while flexibility is a prerequisite in football, the extent of the changes required for this international cycle was notable.
summary: Thomas Tuchel's England squad for the Nations League window includes only 12 players who were available during the World Cup due to injuries. Alex Scott, Lewis Hall, and Myles Lewis-Skelly are highlighted as key beneficiaries of these changes.
author: Guardian Sport

title: FA suspends six‑week ban for Southampton coach Tonda Eckert, imposes £28,000 fine
content:
The Football Association has issued a verdict on Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert’s alleged spying on opponents. The decision follows a long‑running investigation that began after the club’s victory over Middlesbrough in the second leg of May’s Championship playoff semi‑final.

During the post‑match press conference at St Mary’s, Northern Echo journalist Dominic Shaw asked, “Hi Tonda, are you a cheat?” The question prompted Eckert to walk out of the session. Eckert subsequently admitted to authorising the spying, a fact that had put England’s football authorities in a difficult position over the appropriate punishment.

The FA’s autumn ruling gives Eckert a six‑week ban that is suspended until the end of the 2027‑28 season, a £28,000 fine and a formal reprimand. The decision concludes the investigation into the incident.
summary: Southampton manager Tonda Eckert admitted authorising spying on opponents after the club beat Middlesbrough in the Championship playoff semi‑final second leg. The FA issued a six‑week ban suspended until the end of the 2027‑28 season, a £28,000 fine and a reprimand.

title: Tillis criticizes Trump advisers for work with pro-Russian Bosnia group
content:
Retiring Senator Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) on Wednesday criticized two consultants to President Trump for receiving significant profits from their work advising a pro-Russian government in the Balkans during the U.S. midterm elections cycle. The report details the financial gains these advisers earned while working with the entity identified as Republika Srpska.

Tillis, who serves as co-chair of the Senate NATO Observer Group, described Republika Srpska as a “destabilizing force” in his condemnation of the advisers’ activities.
summary: Retiring Sen. Thom Tillis condemned a report that two consultants to President Trump received a large profit from advising a pro-Russian government in the Balkans. The senator, who serves as co-chair of the Senate NATO Observer Group, called Republika Srpska a “destabilizing force.”

title: Don Lemon says there's a 65-70 percent chance he runs for president
content:
Former CNN anchor and media personality Don Lemon stated that there is a 65 to 70 percent chance he will run for president of the United States. Lemon acknowledged that he has considered entering the race, placing his likelihood of doing so at greater than 50 percent.

He noted that he is currently focused on his existing commitments, stating, “I never say never. I’ve got a lot on my plate right now doing what I’m doing.”
summary: Former CNN anchor Don Lemon states he has considered running for president and puts the likelihood at over 50 percent. He noted that he has a lot on his plate right now with his current activities.

title: Trump rallies in San Antonio as Texas Senate and governor races heat up
content:
President Trump returned to Texas on Wednesday night to hold a rally in San Antonio, focusing on the state’s highly competitive Senate and gubernatorial races. The event, which began at 7 p.m., featured Senate candidate Ken as part of the GOP campaign gathering.

These two marquee contests are expected to be among the most closely watched in this year’s midterm elections.
summary: President Trump returned to Texas Wednesday night to hold a rally in San Antonio. The state's Senate and governor races are shaping up to be among the most competitive in this year's midterm elections.

title: Burnham to hold security talks with German chancellor in Berlin
content:
Downing Street announced that Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s deputy, Andy Burnham, will hold security talks with the German Chancellor in Berlin. The meeting is scheduled to take place during Burnham’s first official visit to Germany.

According to the Prime Minister’s residence, the agenda will focus on deepening cooperation between the two nations. This collaboration is intended to address rising hybrid threats posed by Russia.
summary: Downing Street stated that deeper cooperation against rising hybrid threats from Russia would be a key agenda item. This topic will feature during Burnham's first official visit to Germany.

title: Study links pre-pregnancy HPV vaccine to lower risk of preterm birth
content: A large Swedish study published in The BMJ indicates that receiving the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine before pregnancy is associated with a lower risk of major pregnancy complications, including preterm birth. The research found that the reduction in risk was more significant among women who were vaccinated at an earlier age.
summary: A large Swedish study published in The BMJ found that receiving the HPV vaccine before pregnancy is associated with a lower risk of major pregnancy complications, including preterm birth. The study noted that the reduction in risk was greater among women who were vaccinated at an earlier age.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds RSV maternal vaccine cuts baby disease risk by 74% but uptake is low
content:
A new review indicates that vaccinating against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) during pregnancy reduces the risk of severe disease in infants by 74%. Despite this significant benefit, the report notes that vaccine uptake remains low in many countries.

The study highlights disparities in vaccination rates, finding lower uptake among specific socioeconomic and ethnic groups, individuals with reduced access to healthcare, and younger mothers.
summary: A new review indicates that vaccinating against respiratory syncytial virus during pregnancy lowers the risk of severe disease in babies by 74%. The report reveals that vaccine uptake remains low in many countries, particularly among certain socioeconomic and ethnic groups, those with reduced health care access, and younger mothers.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Intranasal sufentanil-ketamine effective for pediatric acute pain
content:
Intranasal sufentanil-ketamine has been identified as a fast-acting treatment that appears safe and effective for managing acute pain in pediatric patients within emergency departments. These findings were reported in a study presented at the annual European Emergency Medicine Congress, which took place in Paris from September 23 to 27.

The research indicates that the medication is well tolerated by children and successfully curbs acute pain, offering a viable option for emergency care settings.
summary: A study presented at the European Emergency Medicine Congress found intranasal sufentanil-ketamine to be fast-acting and well tolerated. The treatment appears effective at reducing acute pain for pediatric patients in the emergency department.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Protein LMOD1 offers new clues to muscle regeneration
content:
Skeletal muscle regeneration relies on muscle stem cells, which typically remain in a quiescent state within healthy resting tissue. Following an injury, these cells are activated and begin to proliferate before differentiating into specialized skeletal muscle cells. This process enables the formation of new or repaired muscle fibers.

The regenerative process involves the fusion of these newly developed cells with one another or with existing muscle fibers. Protein LMOD1 has been identified as offering new clues to this mechanism, highlighting its potential role in understanding how skeletal muscles repair themselves after damage.
summary: Skeletal muscles regenerate after injury through the activation of quiescent muscle stem cells. These cells proliferate, differentiate into specialized skeletal muscle cells, and fuse to generate new or repaired muscle fibers.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Levi Strauss raises profit forecast after tariff refunds, sales outlook muted
content:
Levi Strauss on Wednesday posted earnings that beat expectations, citing benefits from tariff refunds.

The company has raised its profit guidance following the refunds, indicating stronger profitability for the period.

Despite the improved earnings outlook, Levi Strauss said its sales outlook remains less optimistic.
summary: Levi Strauss posted earnings on Wednesday that beat expectations and benefited from tariff refunds. The company lifted its profit guidance while offering a less optimistic sales outlook.

title: P. aeruginosa uses two protein plugs to seal channels against antibiotics
content:
A joint research team has identified a new mechanism underlying antibiotic resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a major multidrug-resistant "superbug." The study reveals that the bacterium uses two protein plugs to seal channels, thereby protecting itself against antibiotics.

This discovery provides important clues for the development of new treatments for multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. The findings have been published in the journal Nature Communications.
summary: A joint research team identified a new mechanism for antibiotic resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa involving two protein plugs that seal channels. The findings, published in Nature Communications, provide clues for developing new treatments for multidrug-resistant infections.

title: Study: International experience boosts business leader performance
content:
A new study published in the Journal of Management indicates that business leaders with international experience play a significant role in shaping organizational success. The research associates these leaders with stronger overall organizational performance.

Specifically, the study links international experience among business leaders to higher growth, increased profitability, and improved stock market performance.
summary: A new study in the Journal of Management finds that business leaders with international experience are associated with stronger organizational performance. This includes higher growth, profitability, and stock market performance for their organizations.
author: Phys.org

title: UMBC researcher reveals how Pseudomonas aeruginosa senses iron to alter metabolism
content:
Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a common cause of hospital-acquired infections that is increasingly resistant to antibiotics, utilizes a specific mechanism to sense iron. New research reveals how a two-protein system within the bacterium functions as a sensitive switch to detect the presence of iron both outside and inside the cell.

The study, conducted by Aaron Smith, professor of chemistry and biochemistry at UMBC, and collaborators at Oklahoma State University, demonstrates that this protein pair triggers significant changes in the microbe’s metabolism upon detecting iron. These findings provide insight into the bacterium's adaptive capabilities, which are relevant to efforts aimed at fighting such infections.
summary: New research by Aaron Smith at UMBC and collaborators shows that Pseudomonas aeruginosa uses a two-protein system to detect iron inside and outside the cell. This mechanism acts like a sensitive switch that rewrites large parts of the bacterium's metabolism in response to iron levels.
author: Phys.org

title: Baltic Sea microorganisms aid carbon transport to depths
content:
A new study from the Department of Ecology, Environment and Plant Sciences at Stockholm University reveals that tiny photosynthetic organisms in the Baltic Sea play a significant role in moving carbon from surface waters to the sea's depths. The research highlights that these organisms contribute substantially to this vertical carbon transport.

The study identifies the ability of these photosynthetic organisms to form colonies and aggregates as a critical factor determining how much of their biomass sinks. This aggregation process influences the efficiency of carbon transfer from the surface to deeper parts of the Baltic Sea.
summary: A new study from Stockholm University indicates that tiny photosynthetic organisms in the Baltic Sea contribute substantially to moving carbon from surface waters to deeper parts of the sea. The research shows that these organisms' ability to form colonies and aggregates is a key factor determining how much of their biomass sinks.
author: Phys.org

title: Cost of Canadian wildfires could top $2 trillion over the 21st century, study shows
content:
A new study from Simon Fraser University estimates that the cost of Canadian wildfires could exceed $2 trillion over the 21st century. The research highlights that failing to curb global warming now could result in trillions of dollars in wildfire impacts for future generations of Canadians.

This study is noted as being among the first to assign a specific price tag to projected Canadian wildfire activity that is driven by climate change.
summary: Failure to curb global warming now could cost future generations of Canadians trillions of dollars in wildfire impacts alone, according to a new Simon Fraser University study. The study is among the first to put a price tag on projected Canadian wildfire activity driven by climate change.
author: Phys.org

title: Snowball Earth iron deposits may have formed via microbes without sunlight
content:
Iron is one of the most abundant metals on Earth's surface, but the formation of massive iron ore deposits throughout geological history has long remained a mystery. The prevailing scientific theory suggests that ancient photosynthetic bacteria oxidized iron, causing it to precipitate and accumulate in the oceans.

New perspectives on this process propose that these deposits may have formed through the activity of microbes living without sunlight during the Snowball Earth era.
summary: Research suggests that massive iron ore deposits from the Snowball Earth era may have formed through microbes living without sunlight. This challenges the prevailing theory that ancient photosynthetic bacteria oxidized iron to create these deposits.
author: Phys.org

title: Optogenetic gene therapy safely restores partial sight in blind people
content:
Researchers have revealed that a type of gene therapy known as optogenetic therapy is safe and can partly restore sight in blind people. The approach is based on Nobel prize-winning science and utilizes a technique for turning nerve cells on and off using light.

This specific technique for manipulating nerve cells with light recently received the 2026 Nobel prize in physiology or medicine.
summary: Researchers revealed that optogenetic gene therapy is safe and can partly restore sight in blind people. The approach uses Nobel prize-winning science to turn nerve cells on and off using light.

title: Android Navigation Buttons Return to Googlebooks Keyboard
content:
Googlebooks feature a new keyboard design that repurposes the F1, F2, and F3 keys to display the triangle, circle, and square navigation icons originally introduced in Android 5.0 Lollipop. These symbols historically represented the back, home, and app switcher buttons on Android devices before the industry shifted toward gesture-based navigation.

The article clarifies that the Quick Insert and Google logo keys are not new additions, having first appeared on some Chromebooks a couple of years ago. While the physical navigation icons are a nod to older Android interfaces, they remain available as an alternative on modern phones, including those running Android 17.

title: BMW’s iX4 SUV is a 428-mile defensive weapon against China’s EV takeover
content:

The vehicle is the third entry in BMW’s next-generation Neue Klasse lineup, joining the previously released iX3 and i3. The company is positioning this new lineup as a defensive strategy against the growing market share of Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers.

The initial release of the iX4 50 xDrive is scheduled for March 2027, with a higher-performance M60 xDrive version planned for later in the same year. BMW emphasizes the vehicle’s advanced technology and drive quality as key features in its effort to retain customers in the competitive electric vehicle market.
summary: While much of the automotive world sits dumbfounded as China gobbles up all its customers, BMW continues to roll out extremely well-crafted, technologically advanced electric vehicles that impress in both drive quality and price. The latest is the BMW iX4, a coupe-shaped SUV that puts a sportier spin on the automaker's iX3.

title: TP-Link Faces US Sales Block as FCC Router Ban Persists
content:
TP‑Link is unable to sell its latest routers in the United States because the company still requires an exemption from the Federal Communications Commission’s router ban.  

The ban, which is part of a broader regulatory push that has led to lawsuits in four states, has left TP‑Link without the ability to offer its newest products in the U.S. market until the exemption is granted.
summary: TP-Link is unable to sell its newest routers in the United States. The company still requires an exemption from the FCC's router ban.
author: Ars Technica

title: Opus Builds Ambitious, Free Creative Cloud Alternatives Targeting Adobe
content: A bold AI developer has announced a new wave of open‑source alternatives to Adobe’s Creative Cloud, declaring that “software is over.” The developer’s project, built by Opus, positions its clones as ambitious and free, but notes that the products are nowhere near finished. The initiative directly challenges Adobe’s dominance in creative software by offering cost‑free, community‑driven options.
summary: Opus, a bold AI developer, has released open source Creative Cloud alternatives targeting Adobe. The projects are ambitious, free, and still far from finished.
author: Ars Technica

title: Microsoft unveils Surface Laptop Ultra AI PCs powered by Nvidia chips
content:
Microsoft has announced a new line of AI‑powered PCs called the Surface Laptop Ultra. The devices run on Nvidia chips that are specifically engineered to execute AI models and agents.  

During the reveal, Microsoft disclosed the specifications and pricing for the Surface Laptop Ultra. The PCs are also set to run a revamped version of Windows 11.  

No additional details were provided in the announcement.
summary: Microsoft revealed the specs and price for its Surface Laptop Ultra AI PCs. These PCs run on Nvidia chips designed to run AI models and agents.
author: TechCrunch

title: Endeavor Catalyst raises $320M to support founders outside Silicon Valley
content:
Endeavor Catalyst has raised $320 million to continue backing founders outside Silicon Valley. The move comes as venture capital firms increasingly focus on the San Francisco area.

Half of the profits from the new funding will be returned to the nonprofit that identifies and supports these founders.
summary: Endeavor Catalyst raised $320 million to continue backing founders outside Silicon Valley. Half of the profits are returned to the nonprofit that finds them.
author: TechCrunch

title: Mecka AI nabs $60M from Sequoia for robot training data
content:
Mecka AI, a startup that collects and analyzes human motion data to train humanoid robots and other kinds of robots, has secured a $60 million investment from Sequoia Capital.

The company pays people to record everyday tasks, using the resulting data to improve robot training and performance.
summary: Mecka AI collects and analyzes human motion data to train humanoid robots and other kinds of robots. The startup pays people to record everyday tasks.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI says teen ChatGPT use limited; research calls risk unacceptable
content:
OpenAI has stated that the use of ChatGPT by teenagers is limited.  

Research evaluating teen interactions with the tool concluded that the associated risk is “unacceptable,” noting that key safeguards intended to protect young users frequently failed.  

The findings highlight concerns about the effectiveness of existing guardrails for adolescent users of the AI service.
summary: OpenAI says teen use of ChatGPT is limited. Research found that important guardrails for teens using ChatGPT often failed, deeming the risk unacceptable.
author: BBC Technology

title: Fuel prices added to Google Maps as petrol and diesel costs soar
content:
Google Maps has incorporated fuel price information, reflecting rising petrol and diesel costs. The update allows users searching for forecourts to see current pricing directly on the map.

The feature uses the government's Fuel Finder scheme to pull price data into the search results. This change aims to give drivers more transparency as fuel prices continue to climb.
summary: Google Maps now shows fuel prices for forecourts. The feature uses the government's Fuel Finder scheme.
author: BBC Technology

title: South African civil groups oppose expansion of electricity‑heavy data centres
content:
Witnesses in Ethiopia’s Tigray region report that Eritrean troops have moved into the area, a claim that Asmara has rejected. The report was highlighted in tonight’s edition of the news briefing.

Separately, the African Union announced the launch of the Africa Credit Rating Agency, which will assess the financial health of African states and companies. The new agency is part of the Union’s broader efforts to strengthen economic oversight on the continent.

In South Africa, civil society groups are opposing the expansion of data centres, citing the large amounts of electricity, water and land they require. The opposition reflects growing concerns over the environmental and resource impacts of the growing data‑centre industry.
summary: South African civil society is pushing back against the expansion of data centres that require vast amounts of electricity, water and land. The African Union has launched the Africa Credit Rating Agency to assess the financial health of African states and companies.
author: France 24

title: French PM Sebastien Lecornu pledges deficit cut to 5% amid student protests
content:
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu addressed the nation amid student protests and volatile bond markets, pledging to tackle France’s public debt. He said the education ministry had not faced any cuts in the budget proposal presented last week, while emphasizing the need to reduce the public deficit to 5 %.

Lecornu’s remarks came as concerns over France’s spending and debt grew, with the International Monetary Fund urging the country to “get your house in order.” He also announced the release of 10 million barrels of diesel fuel as part of the government’s response.
summary: Lecornu told the nation that the education ministry saw no cuts in the latest budget proposal and said the government must reduce the public deficit to 5%. He also sought to calm student protesters and bond markets while confirming the release of 10 million barrels of diesel fuel amid IMF concerns over France’s spending and debt.
author: France 24

title: France suspends police stun grenades at student protests after pupil loses hand
content:
France announced on Wednesday that police will no longer use stun grenades at student‑led demonstrations, a decision announced by the interior minister amid growing allegations of police brutality. The move follows an incident in which a pupil lost a hand during recent protests.

The suspension comes after days of sometimes violent demonstrations across the country, during which tens of thousands of people marched on Tuesday to demand better conditions in high schools. FRANCE 24’s Monte Francis reported the policy change.
summary: France has suspended the use of stun grenades by police at student-led demonstrations, the interior minister said on Wednesday. Tens of thousands of people protested across France on Tuesday demanding better conditions in high schools.
author: France 24

title: WHO seeks more information from Russia on suspected pneumonic plague case
content:
The World Health Organization is asking Russia for additional information about a suspected pneumonic plague case that has drawn global attention.  

A WHO senior official said on Wednesday that the agency does not know how a laboratory worker in Siberia died and urged Russian authorities to provide further details. The death has raised worldwide concerns about the possible presence of pneumonic plague.  

The remarks were reported by Monte Francis for France 24.
summary: A top WHO official said Wednesday the agency does not know how a lab worker in Siberia died. She urged Russia to provide more information about the case that prompted global concerns about suspected pneumonic plague.
author: France 24

title: Israel commemorates third anniversary of Hamas Oct. 7 attack amid election campaign
content:
Israel marked the third anniversary of Hamas’s October 7 attack on Wednesday with silent tributes across the country as political debate intensified ahead of upcoming elections. Families gathered at the Nova festival site and at Kfar Aza kibbutz to observe the day.

At the same time, Israeli forces carried out renewed strikes on Gaza. Gaza officials reported that the attacks killed five people, despite the existence of a year‑old ceasefire agreement.
summary: Israel marked the third anniversary of Hamas’s October 7 attack on Wednesday with silent tributes and renewed strikes on Gaza as political debate intensified ahead of elections. Families gathered at the Nova festival site and Kfar Aza kibbutz, and Gaza officials said the strikes killed five people despite a year‑old ceasefire agreement.
author: France 24

title: Thousands march in Rio to protest Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of Brazil runoff
content:
Thousands of people joined a student march in downtown Rio de Janeiro on Wednesday to protest against Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of Brazil’s October 25 presidential runoff.  

The demonstrators, rallying behind incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, voiced opposition to a potential far‑right return to power after Bolsonaro led Sunday’s first‑round vote.
summary: Thousands of people joined a student march in downtown Rio de Janeiro on Wednesday to protest against Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of Brazil's October 25 presidential runoff. Demonstrators rallied behind incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and opposed a far‑right return to power after Bolsonaro led Sunday's first‑round vote.
author: France 24

title: Netanyahu remains Israel's prime minister three years after Oct. 7 attacks
content:
Israel remains under the leadership of Benjamin Netanyahu three years after the October 7 attacks, despite early predictions that the right‑wing premier would soon fall from power. In the immediate aftermath of what officials described as the country’s worst day of bloodshed, pundits in 2023 forecasted a rapid demise for the prime minister.

On the third anniversary of the Hamas‑led assault, Israel has yet to fully address the security lapses of that day, the underlying causes of the attack, or the ensuing war of vengeance, according to the commentary. Netanyahu continues to serve as prime minister and is described as having a “fair shot” at re‑election.

Even if the Likud leader were to be defeated in a vote scheduled for October 27, the analysis notes that his principal rivals in the forthcoming general election do not propose a radical shift in policy toward the Palestinians.
summary: Three years after the October 7 Hamas attack, Benjamin Netanyahu is still Israel's prime minister. Despite earlier predictions of his quick political demise, he retains a fair chance at re‑election, and his main rivals do not call for a radical shift on Palestinian policy.
author: France 24

title: Democratic National Committee sues Trump administration over $12M taxpayer-funded TV ads
content:
The Democratic National Committee filed a lawsuit against President Donald Trump’s administration on Wednesday, challenging the use of taxpayer money for television advertisements that promote the president’s political message.

The complaint alleges that the ads constitute illegal government propaganda and seeks to stop federal funding for the campaign. According to AdImpact, more than $12 million has been spent on the ads, which have aired in the run‑up to November’s midterm elections.

The DNC’s legal action comes as the midterm election season approaches.
summary: The Democratic National Committee filed a lawsuit against President Donald Trump’s administration on Wednesday, alleging the government’s taxpayer-funded television ads illegally promote his political message. The suit seeks to stop federal funding for the ads, which have cost more than $12 million to air ahead of the November midterm elections, according to AdImpact.
author: France 24

title: Trump campaigns heavily before midterms, spending at taxpayers' expense
content:
Donald Trump, who is not listed on any ballot, is intensifying his campaign efforts as the United States prepares for the upcoming midterm elections. His unusually aggressive tactics and promises are being funded largely at the expense of U.S. taxpayers.

Legal analysts caution that some of the methods and commitments being employed could run afoul of federal law, according to experts cited in the report.
summary: Trump is campaigning hard ahead of the upcoming midterm elections even though he is not on the ballot. Experts say his tactics and promises, which have largely been at the expense of US taypayers, might violate federal law.
author: DW World

title: Thousands march in Rio protesting Flavio Bolsonaro after his presidential run‑off advance
content:
Thousands of students and other demonstrators gathered in Rio de Janeiro to protest against Flavio Bolsonaro, using the chant “No to the father, no to the son.” The rally followed Flavio Bolsonaro’s advancement to Brazil’s presidential run‑off.

Organizers directed their criticism at the younger Bolsonaro, linking him to his father’s political legacy. The march highlighted public opposition to his candidacy as the election moves toward its final round.
summary: Students and other protesters marched in Rio against Flavio Bolsonaro. The march took place after Flavio Bolsonaro advanced to Brazil's presidential run‑off.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces claim advances in western Taiz mountain belt
content:
Yemeni forces backed by Saudi Arabia said they have captured key heights in western Taiz’s mountain belt that overlooks the coast, as Houthi attacks continue.  

The claim of advances comes from the western part of Taiz province, where the forces say they have moved forward in the mountainous area that dominates the coastal view.
summary: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces say they have captured key heights in the western Taiz mountain belt overlooking the coast. Houthi attacks continue.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Spanish pensioner Maricarmen Abascal, 87, dies after eviction that sparked protests
content:
Spanish pensioner Maricarmen Abascal, 87, has died, a union said. Her death follows the high‑profile eviction that sparked protests across the country.

Abascal was forcibly removed on a stretcher from the apartment she had lived in for more than 70 years in September, an incident that ignited nationwide demonstrations.
summary: Union officials said 87‑year‑old Maricarmen Abascal has died. She was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years in September, an eviction that triggered nationwide protests.
author: BBC World

title: Verstappen's Sepang win seen as warning to Red Bull rivals
content:
Max Verstappen’s victory in Sepang has been hailed as a warning to Red Bull’s rivals, writes Giles Richards. The win followed significant improvements to the car, allowing the Dutchman to drive a competitive machine and secure a dominant triumph for Red Bull.

Verstappen expressed pleasure at finally being able to drive a car he was comfortable with, a contrast to earlier in the season when the vehicle had been a handful and had caused his title hopes to fade. The transformation is seen as laying the groundwork for renewed success next season.

The article also notes the importance of Verstappen’s triumph emerging from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, underscoring the significance of the Sepang victory. The piece was written by Giles Richards.
summary: Max Verstappen took a dominant victory at Sepang driving a competitive Red Bull car. The win, attributed to recent car improvements, is portrayed as a warning to Red Bull’s rivals and a sign of renewed success for the team next season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Southampton manager Tonda Eckert given six-week suspended ban for Spygate
content:
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has received a six-week suspended ban and a £28,000 fine for his involvement in the Spygate scandal. The independent commission imposed the sanction after Eckert admitted all charges of misconduct, citing his "genuine contrition." The scandal previously resulted in Southampton’s expulsion from the Championship playoff final, denying the club a chance at Premier League promotion.

The Football Association (FA) had sought a stricter penalty, with its lawyers demanding a three-month ban from all football. The FA has indicated it may appeal against the independent commission's decision regarding Eckert's suspended ban.
summary: An independent commission issued Tonda Eckert a six-week suspended ban and a £28,000 fine after he admitted all misconduct charges. The FA, which sought a three-month ban, may appeal the decision.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tuchel says England embrace calculated risks after Nations League wins
content:
Thomas Tuchel believes the England national team has reached a new level after implementing tactical adjustments during their opening Nations League matches. The head coach stated that he wanted players to maintain their aggressive high press while also allowing them greater freedom to trust their instincts and cover for teammates. Tuchel noted that the squad has embraced these "calculated risks," with the manager expressing satisfaction that everyone bought into the new ideas.

Following an initial loss to Spain at Wembley, England secured three consecutive victories, including two against Czechia and a 7-0 win over Croatia in Rijeka. These results have effectively guaranteed England’s progression to the quarter-finals of the competition, which is viewed as a preparation phase for Euro 2028. The recent success also helps the team move past their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Midfielder Jarell Quansah expressed confidence in the team’s current form, stating, “We can really dominate teams.”
summary: Thomas Tuchel claims England have unlocked a new level by balancing aggression with greater freedom in their play. The team recorded three wins in the Nations League, including a 7-0 victory over Croatia, to guarantee a quarter-final place.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Saracens' Venter criticizes Prem Rugby as autocratic over media duties
content:
Saracens technical director and head of culture Brendan Venter has criticized the administration of Prem Rugby, describing it as an “autocracy” during a recent public appearance at the club’s training base. Venter, who initially appeared reluctant to speak, engaged in a lengthy discussion that contrasted rugby with winemaking and argued that media interviews “steal my joy.”

The technical director’s remarks extended beyond club management, touching on broader geopolitical issues including Ukraine and Gaza. He also recounted delivering an inspirational talk at a local school, offering a multifaceted perspective to the audience present at the event.
summary: Saracens technical director Brendan Venter described Prem Rugby as an autocracy during a public appearance at the club's training base. He stated that interviews steal his joy while comparing rugby to winemaking and discussing topics including Ukraine and Gaza.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jon Rahm exit from LIV Golf expected to trigger mass player exodus
content:
The withdrawal of Saudi funding has led the LIV Golf tour to file for bankruptcy, a move that is expected to trigger a mass exodus of players from the breakaway circuit. A bankruptcy hearing held on Wednesday revealed that Jon Rahm’s lawyer described the proposed terms for "LIV 2.0" as "unacceptable," indicating that the Spaniard will soon depart from the tour. Rahm, who joined LIV in 2023, is set to play no part in the organization’s post-Saudi Arabian form.

Rahm’s departure is considered a significant blow to the tour, which continues to operate with the hope of remaining a going concern. The news suggests that other high-profile players, including Tyrrell Hatton, are likely to follow Rahm in leaving the stricken circuit.
summary: Jon Rahm will not participate in LIV Golf after a bankruptcy hearing revealed unacceptable terms proposed by the tour. His departure is expected to prompt other major players, including Tyrrell Hatton, to leave the circuit.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England Seek Replacement for Harry Kane as Career Reaches End
content: Harry Kane’s record-breaking career with the England national team cannot continue indefinitely, raising questions about the future of the squad’s primary striker. The central issue for the Three Lions is whether a ready-made replacement for Kane has already emerged or if the player is yet to be identified.
summary: Harry Kane's record-breaking England career cannot continue forever. The Three Lions are looking for a ready-made replacement.
author: BBC Sport

title: Messi's international career ends as Ronaldo's future remains uncertain
content: Lionel Messi is set to conclude his international career with a fond farewell, while Cristiano Ronaldo faces the risk of his tenure ending less gracefully. BBC Sport has examined the potential conclusions of the international careers of these two football icons.
summary: Lionel Messi's international career has concluded with a fond farewell. Cristiano Ronaldo's international career is at risk of ending on a bitter note.
author: BBC Sport

title: BBC Sport analyzes early Premier League table stability after five games
content: With only five matchdays completed, the Premier League standings may appear premature, yet BBC Sport suggests the table is likely more stable than initially assumed. The broadcaster has analyzed statistical data to examine the reliability of the early season rankings.
summary: The Premier League table may be more settled than expected after just five games. BBC Sport examines the statistics behind the current early season standings.
author: BBC Sport

title: Eckert Remains Southampton Boss After Spygate Ban Suspended
content:
Tonda Eckert has been cleared to remain in his position as Southampton manager following a ruling on his involvement in the Spygate incident. The decision allows him to continue his duties without interruption.

Eckert was issued a suspended ban for his role in the controversy, meaning he is free to stay in charge of the team.
summary: Tonda Eckert is permitted to continue as Southampton manager following a decision to suspend his ban. The suspension relates to his involvement in the Spygate incident.
author: BBC Sport

title: Cantwell unveils AI regulatory framework
content:
Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee, unveiled a framework Wednesday for regulating artificial intelligence. The proposal comes amid increasing pressure on lawmakers to address the risks associated with the technology.

Cantwell outlined a set of principles for how Congress and the executive branch should approach AI, arguing that these measures are necessary to manage the risks posed by the technology.
summary: Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee, unveiled a framework for regulating artificial intelligence. She laid out principles for how Congress and the executive branch should approach AI to manage risks.
author: The Hill

title: Trump says 'Trump Accounts' will limit spread of socialism
content:
President Trump stated on Wednesday that his administration’s new investment accounts for children, known as “Trump Accounts,” will have a “huge effect” in reducing positive views of socialism and communism among young Americans. The announcement was made during an event held in the Oval Office to promote the initiative.

According to the president, children will be “watching their accounts” grow until they gain control over them upon reaching a certain age.
summary: President Trump stated that his administration's new investment accounts for children will have a huge effect in reducing positive views of socialism and communism. He made these remarks during an Oval Office event promoting the "Trump Accounts" program.
author: The Hill

title: Rubio calls for new era of US and European power in Athens speech
content:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a major speech in Athens, Greece, on Wednesday, calling for a new era of U.S. and European power on the global stage. The address took place against the dramatic backdrop of the ancient Acropolis and the setting Mediterranean sun.

Rubio stated that the United States and its allies currently stand at a crossroads, emphasizing the need for renewed strength and cooperation between the two regions.
summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a major speech in Athens, Greece, calling for a new era of U.S. and European power on the global stage. He stated that the U.S. and its allies stand at a crossroads while speaking against the backdrop of the ancient Acropolis.
author: The Hill

title: Hegseth presents Presidential Unit Citation to USS Abraham Lincoln crew
content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth presented the Presidential Unit Citation, described as the highest unit award, to the crew of the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group on Wednesday. The ceremony took place as the aircraft carrier returned to the United States following a lengthy deployment in the Middle East.

Hegseth commended the crew for their support of U.S. Military operations against Iran and their role in helping enforce regional security measures.
summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth presented the Presidential Unit Citation to the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group crew upon their return to the U.S. He praised the crew for supporting U.S. Military operations against Iran and helping enforce the region's security.
author: The Hill

title: HBCU students sue Missouri for $549M, citing underfunding
content: Current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri filed a lawsuit on Wednesday, alleging that the state has underfunded the institution for decades. The plaintiffs are seeking nearly $549 million from the state, which they intend to direct toward a fund for campus repairs and other university needs. The legal action centers on a state law that mandates specific financial allocations to the university.
summary: Current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri filed a lawsuit alleging the state has underfunded the institution for decades. The students are seeking almost $549 million to be paid into a fund for campus repairs and other university needs.
author: The Hill

title: Trump dismisses query on cash giveaways before midterms, touts tariffs and growth
content:
President Trump dismissed a question regarding his administration’s distribution of funds to Americans prior to the midterm elections, shifting the focus to his economic policies. During a Wednesday interview in the Oval Office with The Independent’s Andrew, the president emphasized the administration's economic performance in response to the inquiry.

Instead of addressing the specific question about pre-election cash distributions, Trump touted the impact of his tariffs. He stated, “What we’re doing is we have tremendous growth. We have the greatest growth of any country, maybe ever in history.”
summary: President Trump on Wednesday dismissed a question about his administration sending money to Americans ahead of the midterms. He instead highlighted tariffs and claimed the United States is experiencing unprecedented growth while speaking in the Oval Office.
author: The Hill

title: Trump approved the military's 1st firing squad execution since WWII. Why now?
content:
The Pentagon announced that Nidal Hasan will be executed by firing squad in December at Fort Hood. This marks the first military firing squad execution since World War II. Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people at the same base in 2009.

The decision to use a firing squad followed a botched lethal injection in Tennessee. The announcement highlights a shift in execution methods within the military justice system.
summary: The Pentagon says Nidal Hasan will be executed by firing squad in December at Fort Hood, where he killed 13 people in 2009. The announcement came days after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.
author: NPR Politics

title: Greens investigate party member behind Zionism motion
content: Lubna Speitan, a member of the Greens party, is facing an investigation after court documents revealed she was listed as a "close friend" of a man who was subsequently jailed for supporting al-Qaeda. The party is currently examining the circumstances surrounding this connection and its impact on her membership.
summary: It has emerged Lubna Speitan was listed in court documents as a "close friend" of a man later jailed for supporting al-Qaeda.
author: BBC Politics

title: Study links gut inflammation to food reactions in IBD patients
content: A new study set to be published in Gastroenterology suggests that gut inflammation alters how gut bacteria break down food, potentially triggering immune reactions to foods that were previously tolerated. The research aims to clarify why many individuals with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) experience adverse reactions to specific foods, such as dairy or gluten, even during periods of remission.
summary: A study to be published in Gastroenterology finds that gut inflammation alters how gut bacteria break down food, potentially triggering immune reactions. The findings may explain why people with inflammatory bowel disease react to foods like dairy or gluten even during remission.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Phthalate byproducts affect multiple cell types in human ovarian tissue
content: A new study from Karolinska Institutet, published in the journal eBioMedicine, indicates that common chemicals known as phthalates may affect several different cell types in the human ovary. These chemicals are widely used in plastics, cosmetics, and personal care products.
summary: A new study from Karolinska Institutet indicates that phthalates may affect several different cell types in the human ovary. The research was published in the journal eBioMedicine.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study links higher physical activity to slower Parkinson's progression
content:
A new study published in Neurology found that higher levels of physical activity are associated with slower declines in thinking and memory, as well as slower worsening of movement symptoms, among people with Parkinson's disease. The research highlights a link between increased physical activity and a more gradual progression of the condition.

The study authors noted that the findings do not establish that physical activity causes slower disease progression. Instead, the results demonstrate an association between the two factors.
summary: A new study in Neurology found that people with Parkinson's disease who engaged in higher levels of physical activity experienced slower declines in thinking, memory, and movement symptoms. The researchers note that the study shows an association rather than proving that physical activity causes slower disease progression.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Mysterious Papua New Guinea rock reveals unexpected cooling as it descended deeper underground
content:
Scientists report that a mysterious rock from Papua New Guinea revealed unexpected cooling as it moved deeper underground, a finding that challenges current models of heat distribution within the Earth. This discovery impacts the scientific understanding of how thermal energy is managed deep inside the planet.

The new data has potential implications for interpreting geological processes, including the mechanisms behind earthquakes, volcanic activity, and the movement of carbon through Earth's interior.
summary: The discovery of an unexpectedly hot rock beneath Earth's surface is challenging scientists' understanding of how heat is distributed deep inside the planet, with potential implications for how they understand earthquakes, volcanic activity and the…
author: Phys.org

title: Michigan officials see benefits but cost concerns over nine‑day early voting
content:
A University of Michigan survey finds that while most city and township officials in Michigan view recent state election administration reforms as having a positive or neutral impact, many small communities are feeling pressure from the nine‑day early in‑person voting period.

Officials cite the costs and staffing demands required to support the extended early voting window as a primary concern. The survey highlights the strain on resources in smaller municipalities despite the overall favorable assessment of the reforms.
summary: Most Michigan city and township officials say recent state election administration reforms have had positive or neutral impacts. However, many note that nine days of early in‑person voting creates cost and staffing challenges, according to a University of Michigan survey.
author: Phys.org

title: Enzymes could unlock biological recycling of difficult plastic waste
content: Plastics are durable, inexpensive materials that have become integral to daily life, with global production exceeding 400 million metric tons annually. Despite their widespread use, a significant portion of these materials is insufficiently recycled, leading to a growing environmental burden from plastic waste.
summary: They are durable, cheap and everyday life is now hardly imaginable without them: plastics. More then 400 million metric tons are produced every year.
author: Phys.org

title: Polymer coating improves MXene stability for CO2-to-methane conversion
content: A research team has developed a photocatalytic technology designed to enhance the stability of MXene, an emerging material known for its vulnerability to water. The primary goal of this innovation is to enable the efficient conversion of carbon dioxide into methane.
summary: A research team developed a photocatalytic technology that enhances the water stability of MXene. This innovation allows the material to efficiently convert carbon dioxide into methane.
author: Phys.org

title: Jacob Aron recommends Kevin Roose's book The AGI Chronicles as an AI primer
content: Jacob Aron recommends The AGI Chronicles by Kevin Roose as a primer for the fast-moving field of artificial intelligence. Aron notes that while he and Roose disagree on when or if AI will achieve human-level intelligence, the book still serves as a useful resource for those unfamiliar with the topic.
summary: Jacob Aron recommends Kevin Roose's book The AGI Chronicles as a primer to a fast-moving field. This recommendation is made despite disagreements over when or if AI will achieve human-level intelligence.
author: New Scientist

title: 194-year-old tortoise Jonathan's DNA repair systems linked to exceptional longevity
content: Researchers have analyzed the genome of Jonathan, a 194-year-old giant tortoise residing on St Helena island. The study aims to understand the biological mechanisms that have allowed him to live for more than double the average life expectancy of his species.
summary: The genome of Jonathan, a 194-year-old giant tortoise resident of St Helena island, has been probed to understand his longevity. His DNA contains exceptional repair systems that fight off ageing, allowing him to live more than double his species' average life expectancy.
author: New Scientist

title: MIT Researchers Build Cloud Platform for Massachusetts Shellfishing Data
content: MIT researchers have developed a cloud-based platform designed to assist Massachusetts coastal towns and the state in managing shellfishing closures. The new tool aims to provide thousands of permit holders with a clearer understanding of specific areas where they are authorized to fish.
summary: MIT researchers developed a cloud-based platform to assist Massachusetts coastal towns and the state in managing shellfishing closures. The tool provides thousands of permit holders with a clearer view of where they can fish.
author: MIT News

title: DNA analysis of 194-year-old giant tortoise Jonathan reveals longevity secrets
content:
Scientists have analyzed the genetic code of Jonathan, a 194-year-old giant tortoise, to uncover insights into human longevity. The DNA analysis identified specific gene patterns that appear to protect the functioning of mitochondria.

Jonathan, considered the world’s oldest living land animal, resides at Plantation House, the official residence of the governor of Saint Helena in the South Atlantic. At 194 years old, the tortoise is a contemporary of Queen Victoria and Charles Darwin.
summary: Scientists analyzed the genetic code of Jonathan, the world's oldest living land animal, who is believed to be 194 years old. The study identified gene patterns that appear to protect the functioning of mitochondria, offering insights into extending human lifespan.
author: Guardian Science

title: Artemis II Crew Tablet Screenshot Shows Moon Eclipse with Annotations
content:
NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor “Ike” Glover, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, observed impact flashes and their locations during an Artemis II mission. The crew members recorded their observations using handwritten notes on a tablet, with each individual’s annotations distinguished by specific colors: Wiseman in blue, Glover in green, and Hansen in red.

The data was captured in an April 6, 2026, screenshot showing a visualization of a dark Moon eclipsing the Sun. This image serves as a record of the crew’s real-time monitoring of lunar surface activity during the mission.
summary: A screenshot from an Artemis II crew member’s tablet shows a dark Moon eclipsing the Sun with handwritten annotations. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor “Ike” Glover, and CSA Jeremy Hansen recorded impact flashes and their locations.
author: NASA News

title: NASA’s Curiosity Captures View of Gale Crater After 1 km Milestone
content:
NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover captured a view looking back at the floor of Gale Crater on September 5, 2026, the 5,006th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The photo shows the crater’s rim visible in the distance.

Just nine days earlier, on August 26 (Sol 4,996), Curiosity set a mission milestone by reaching 1 kilometer […].

The image illustrates the rover’s perspective as it continues to explore Gale Crater.

title: Developer Releases Pointless, Mostly-Exact Hacker News Clone in Common Lisp
content:
Shawwn has released "sharc," a nearly exact clone of Hacker News available at news.ycombinator.lol, which mirrors the original site's comments and content. The project, written in Common Lisp, took approximately four months of near-daily development, with Shawwn noting that some days involved 16 hours of work. The codebase is open source on GitHub, and the name "sharc" was suggested by Hacker News founder dang, who collaborated on the project.

The primary goal of sharc was to test the limits of Shawwn's programming abilities and replicate the efficiency of the original site. Benchmarks indicate that sharc generates pages only slightly slower than real Hacker News, though Shawwn has not verified its stability under the original site's scale of 24 million daily views. While the original concept involved using AI-generated comments, the current version displays the same comments as the real site, which Shawwn describes as an "art project" and an "extremely efficient port."

Users who are uncomfortable with their comments being copied can claim their accounts on the clone by visiting their profile page, clicking "claim," and entering a six-digit code into their real Hacker News profile. This process allows them to reset their password on the clone and set the "redact" option to "yes" to hide their content. Shawwn noted that the clone is missing only the /ask and /show features, with the rest of the site being a 95% exact recreation that has been running for several months.
summary: A developer released "sharc," a Common Lisp port of Hacker News that replicates the site's comments and features with high performance. The project took four months to build and allows users to claim their accounts to redact their comments on the clone.

title: Canada to indefinitely bar mental illness as sole reason for euthanasia
content:
Canada’s federal government announced on Wednesday that it will move forward with legislation to indefinitely bar people whose sole health condition is a mental illness from accessing physician‑assisted death. The proposal, driven by the ruling Liberal party, is intended to address a growing clash over eligibility for medical assistance in dying (MAID).

Under the current framework, individuals whose only underlying medical condition is a mental illness have already been prohibited from receiving MAID. That prohibition was slated to be lifted in March, but the issue has divided lawmakers who are debating whether to expand the MAID program to include such cases.

Crisis support resources are listed for those in need: Canada’s Crisis Services Canada can be reached at 1.833.456.4566 or by texting 45645 from 4 p.m. to 12 a.m. ET; the U.S. 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available at 988 or via chat at 988lifeline.org; the UK and Ireland Samaritans can be called toll‑free at 116 123; and Australia’s Lifeline is reachable at 13 11 14. Additional international helplines are available through Befrienders.org.

content:

The hallucinogen’s early use in psychiatric research gave way to widespread adoption by the 1960s counterculture movement, while U.S. intelligence agencies conducted clandestine experiments aimed at manipulating behavior.  

Now, the substance is once again being examined in laboratory settings, signaling a renewed interest in its potential applications. LSD makes its way back to the lab.
summary: LSD has been involved in psychiatric research, counterculture, and secret CIA mind‑control experiments. It is now making its way back to the lab.

title: Saudi Arabia says Houthi airport attacks killed three foreign nationals
content:
Saudi Arabia said that Houthi attacks on airports resulted in the deaths of three foreign nationals. The ministry identified the victims as a Moroccan woman, an Algerian woman and a Sudanese national.

The Moroccan and Algerian women were killed in the city of Abha, while the Sudanese national died in Riyadh.
summary: Saudi Arabia said Houthi attacks on airports killed three foreign nationals. The victims were a Moroccan woman and an Algerian woman in Abha and a Sudanese national in Riyadh.

title: Kenya raises alert after first Ebola death, cites border screening concerns
content:
Kenya has placed the country on high alert after the first Ebola death was reported, prompting officials to step up preparedness measures. The government said it is intensifying its Ebola response amid growing concern that lapses in border screening may have contributed to the fatal case.

Authorities are focusing on strengthening screening procedures at points of entry and enhancing overall readiness to contain further transmission. The heightened vigilance reflects the government's effort to address the identified screening gaps and protect public health.
summary: Kenya’s government has intensified Ebola preparedness efforts. The move follows concern over lapses in border screening after the country’s first Ebola death.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russia's massive overnight barrage kills at least 24 in Ukraine
content:
At least 24 people were killed as Russia launched a massive attack on Ukraine, Ukrainian officials said.

Ukraine reported that the overnight barrage included 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles. The coordinated strike was described as massive by Ukrainian authorities.
summary: At least 24 people were killed as Russia launched a massive attack on Ukraine. Ukraine said the attack used 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and ballistic missiles.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rabbi Dov Lando's anti‑Zionist remarks spark Israel election controversy
content:
Rabbi Dov Lando’s anti‑Zionist remarks have ignited a row ahead of Israel’s election, drawing attention to deep‑seated disputes within the country’s political landscape.  

The rabbi’s comments have highlighted ongoing tensions over Zionism, the issue of conscription for ultra‑Orthodox Jews, and the role of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ultra‑Orthodox allies in the coalition.
summary: Rabbi Dov Lando's anti‑Zionist remarks have stirred an Israel election row. His comments expose tensions over Zionism, conscription and Netanyahu's ultra‑Orthodox allies.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israelis demand accountability for 7 Oct failures, three years after attacks
content:
Israelis are calling for accountability over the failures surrounding the 7 October attacks, three years after the events.  

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has declined to assume personal responsibility for the incident and has refused to order a state inquiry.  

The demand for answers persists despite the prime minister’s refusal to initiate an official investigation.
summary: Israelis are demanding accountability for the failures of the 7 October attacks, three years after the events. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has refused to take personal responsibility or order a state inquiry.
author: BBC World

title: Goodbye Warner, hello Skydance: how will the major merger really impact Hollywood?
content:
Paramount and Warner Bros. have officially merged under the corporate umbrella of Skydance, reducing Hollywood’s major studio count from five to four. The deal, led by billionaire David Ellison, concluded after Skydance outbid Netflix for the century-old studio and overcame legal opposition. Skydance now joins Sony, Disney, and Universal as the remaining major players in the film industry.

The merger extends beyond film production to include the eventual combination of streaming services HBO Max and Paramount+, although no specific timeline has been provided. The combined entity now owns a vast array of television channels, including HBO, Showtime, CBS, MTV, Comedy Central, Cartoon Network, Nickelodeon, TNT, TBS, and CNN.

The inclusion of CNN has drawn particular scrutiny due to recent changes at CBS News, where Bari Weiss’s stewardship has been linked to declines in ratings and prestige for the program 60 Minutes. While Weiss is not expected to oversee CNN and current chair Mark Thompson remains in place, Skydance has stated that CNN will maintain editorial independence. However, concerns persist regarding an oversight board with Ellison appointees, especially given Ellison’s relationship with Donald Trump, who has frequently criticized CNN.
summary: After a windier road than expected, Paramount and Warner are now one, under the banner of Skydance, and the film industry is set for a shake-upHollywood’s big five have officially become the big four. Following a twist-filled saga that saw the century-old studio Warner Bros nearly acquired by the streaming giant Netflix, only to be outbid by Paramount owners Skydance, the company led by billionaire scion David Ellison.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Tom Pidcock furious after police motorbike hits two teammates at Tre Valli Varesine
content:
Tom Pidcock was furious after a police motorcyclist crashed into two of his teammates during the Tre Valli Varesine in Italy, saying he almost quit the race in a rage.  

The incident involved a police motorbike that was traveling the wrong way down the course and struck Pinarello‑Q36.5 riders Camprubí and Gloag, sending them floored in the crash. Pidcock described the event as something that “shouldn’t happen.”  

Despite the chaos, Pidcock finished second in the race. He attributed his frustration to the unexpected collision caused by the police motorcyclist.
summary: Tom Pidcock said he almost quit the Tre Valli Varesine after a police motorbike traveling the wrong way struck his Pinarello Q36.5 teammates Camprubí and Gloag. He finished second in the race.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ronaldo says Jorge Jesus agreed to make eight points on his behalf
content:
Cristiano Ronaldo issued a lengthy statement on Tuesday asserting that Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus had agreed to present eight specific points regarding the player during a press conference before the national team’s match in Denmark last week. Ronaldo claimed he had approved a document outlining these points following a video meeting that included Jesus, his adviser Tiago Craveiro, and Al-Nassr sporting director Simão Coutinho.

The statement indicated that the “validated” notes covered various topics, with mentions made of Pelé, Maradona, loyalty, and selfies. Ronaldo described the process as one where he personally approved the content to be shared by the coach.
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo stated that Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus agreed to make eight points regarding him in a press conference before a game in Denmark. Ronaldo claimed he approved a document listing these points after a video meeting with Jesus, his adviser, and Al-Nassr's sporting director.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pocognoli's Scotland start raises questions over flawed plan and third-place finish
content:
Scotland faces a potential third-place finish in Group B1 of the Nations League, a result that would impact their seeding for Euro 2028 qualifying. This outcome follows the first four matches under manager Sébastien Pocognoli, during which the team has not shown a "manager bounce."

Critics have noted that Ben Gannon-Doak is playing in an odd position while the wider tactical plan appears flawed. These performance issues have raised questions about the current system employed by the national team.
summary: Scotland are facing a third-place finish in Group B1 of the Nations League, which will impact their seeding for Euro 2028 qualifying. The article notes that there has been no new manager bounce under Sébastien Pocognoli and that the wider plan appears flawed.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mikel Arteta signs four-year contract worth over £20m a season
content:
Mikel Arteta has signed a new four-year contract with Arsenal, a deal reportedly worth more than £20m a season that secures his position as the Premier League’s best-paid manager. The agreement extends his tenure at the club, potentially taking his reign beyond a decade if he fulfills the entire term.

The Spanish manager hailed the new deal as “only the beginning” of what he can achieve with the team. The significant pay rise follows his success in leading Arsenal to the league title last season, ending a 22-year wait for the club after three consecutive runner-up finishes.
summary: Mikel Arteta has signed a new four-year contract worth more than £20m a season, making him the best-paid manager in the Premier League. The deal secures his future at Arsenal following their title win after a 22-year wait.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Faf du Plessis questions Canada Super60 T10 format and tiny boundaries
content:
Faf du Plessis questioned the legitimacy of Canada’s “Super60” T10 cricket tournament, stating, “It doesn’t look like proper cricket.” The tournament took place in Vancouver, where players competed in a 50,000-seater stadium that was virtually empty. The event featured extremely short straight boundaries at BC Place, leading to controversial scoring situations, such as a ball traveling 35 meters off the edge of a bat.

During the competition, Mississauga Masters’ Ali Khan bowled a delivery that flew over Toronto Sixers batter Kieron Pollard’s head and crossed the lilliputian straight boundaries. Although the ball landed in the empty stands and was retrieved by a fielder, the shot was technically classified as a five, consisting of a wide plus four, because a six must be struck off the bat. The unusual conditions and sparse attendance have raised questions about the nature of the spectacle.
summary: Faf du Plessis stated that Canada's Super60 tournament does not look like proper cricket due to its extremely small boundaries. The T10 event in Vancouver featured a 50,000-seater stadium with very few spectators, raising questions about the format's spectacle.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Portuguese authorities took 83 days to inform Rui Pinto his witness protection was ending
content:
Portuguese authorities delayed notifying Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto for 83 days regarding the termination of his witness protection status, informing him only ten days before the measures were scheduled to expire. Documents reviewed by the Guardian indicate that the special security programmes commission (CPES), the body overseeing Portugal’s witness protection programme, kept Pinto uninformed of their decision for nearly three months.

The CPES convened on July 8 and 9 to evaluate Pinto’s case and determined that the threat level against him had dropped to low levels. Based on this assessment, the commission concluded that the special protection measures were no longer necessary, leading to the eventual end of his protected witness status.
summary: Portuguese authorities kept Rui Pinto unaware for almost three months that his witness protection status was ending, and they notified him only 10 days before it was due to expire. The special security programmes commission (CPES) met on 8 and 9 July, concluded the threat level against him was low, and determined that special protection measures were no longer warranted.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England faces Twickenham ticket sales slump as Springboks and All Blacks demand outstrips hosts
content:
England is facing a slump in ticket sales for the Nations Championship finals at Twickenham, as demand for matches involving South Africa and New Zealand has outstripped interest in the hosts. This development represents an embarrassing snub for Steve Borthwick’s side, particularly following their 42-21 loss to Ireland in their previous game at the stadium.

The finals weekend will feature six ranking matches at Twickenham next month, with two games scheduled for each day from Friday through Sunday. This event marks the culmination of the competition’s first edition, concluding with a grand finale on Sunday that pits the top nation from the Northern Hemisphere pool against their southern counterparts. The remaining fixtures will match the second-place teams against each other, followed by the third-place teams.
summary: Demand for tickets to the Springboks and All Blacks matches has outstripped that for the host England team during the Nations Championship finals. This ticket sales slump is described as an embarrassing snub for Steve Borthwick’s side following their 42-21 loss to Ireland in the last Twickenham game.
author: Guardian Sport

content: Tom Pidcock expressed his anger and stated he wanted to "stop racing" after two of his team-mates were struck by a police vehicle at the Tre Valli Varesine. The incident occurred when the police vehicle was travelling the wrong way down the race course.
summary: Tom Pidcock said he wanted to stop racing after two teammates were hit by a police vehicle. The vehicle was traveling the wrong way down the course at the Tre Valli Varesine.

title: Senior English Figures Fear Manchester City Could Play Champions League After Relegation
content:
Senior figures in English football have expressed concern that Manchester City could still qualify for the Champions League next season, even if the club is relegated for breaching financial regulations.  

The worry centers on the possibility that the club might be allowed to compete in Europe despite being demoted from the Premier League due to the regulatory breach.
summary: Senior figures in English football are worried that Manchester City could qualify for the Champions League next season. This could happen even if the club is relegated due to breaching financial regulations.

title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan's execution scheduled for December 3
content: Nidal Malik Hasan, convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood mass shooting, is scheduled for execution in December, the U.S. Army announced. A memo released on Tuesday, obtained by NewsNation, specifies the date and time as December 3 at 1 p.m. CDT. The execution will be carried out at Fort Hood.
summary: The U.S. Army has scheduled the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan for December 3 at 1 p.m. CDT. Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood mass shooting.

title: Sarri Singer Calls for Global Action on Terrorism at Oct. 7 Attack's Third Anniversary
content:
On the third anniversary of the Oct. 7 attacks, author Sarri Singer highlighted the continued global indifference to terrorism. In his commentary, Singer argues that the world must confront the universal threat of terrorism by acknowledging it for what it is.

Singer calls for three specific actions: first, to label terrorism accurately; second, to cut off funding to enemy groups; and third, to treat survivor recovery as a matter of national security. He stresses that these steps are essential for addressing the problem on a global scale.
summary: Sarri Singer highlighted the third anniversary of the Oct. 7 attacks, urging the global community to confront terrorism. He called for cutting off enemy funding and treating survivor recovery as a matter of national security.

title: What should teachers teach about the October 7 attacks?
content:
What should teachers teach about the October 7 attacks?

A recent commentary reflects on the challenges of teaching about the October 7 attacks. After three years of listening to how we should teach October 7, the author notes that critics consistently fail to accommodate the complexity of the conflict. The piece underscores the difficulty of presenting a nuanced perspective in educational settings.
summary: After three years of listening to how we should teach October 7, what always strikes me is critics’ utter inability to accommodate the complexity of the conflict.

title: Tillis defends insults in memoir toward Trump officials
content:
Sen. Thom Tillis (R‑NC) defended the harsh remarks he made in his new memoir, saying he stands “by all that.”  The comments, which target Trump administration officials, were read by CNN’s Kaitlan Collins during a Tuesday segment.

Tillis’s book, titled How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents, contains “unsparing” remarks, beginning with a reference to his vote to confirm Defense Secretary Pete.
summary: Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N. C.) defended insults he made in his new memoir toward Trump administration officials. He said he stands by all that, as CNN’s Kaitlan Collins read his unsparing remarks from “How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents,” including his vote to confirm Defense Secretary Pete.

title: OpenAI releases 377 new math breakthroughs on Tuesday
content:
OpenAI announced on Tuesday the release of a new batch of mathematics breakthroughs. The company issued 377 results that span physics, mathematics, and other scientific problems.

The breakthroughs were produced by an internal frontier model that is not yet available to the public. The release follows calls from AI researchers and developers to slow the growth of the technology.

The announcement included the statement: “Towards acceleration of scientific…”.
summary: OpenAI released a new batch of mathematics breakthroughs on Tuesday. The company released 377 results that cover different physics, mathematical and other scientific problems solved by an internal frontier model not yet available to the public.

title: Vance says Iran must make meaningful enrichment reduction to end war
content:
Vice President Kamala Vance told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran must take a “meaningful” step concerning its stockpile of enriched uranium to move forward in nuclear negotiations with the United States.  

Vance said a reduction in Iran’s enrichment activities is essential for progress, noting that Iran’s claim of a right to enrichment remains a key sticking point in talks over its nuclear program.
summary: Vice President Vance told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran must take a meaningful step concerning its enriched uranium stockpile to advance nuclear negotiations with the United States. He said Iran’s claim of a right to enrichment is a key sticking point in the talks.

title: Rand Paul warns Russian plague research could be weaponized
content:
Sen. Rand Paul (R‑Ky.) has voiced concerns that Russia could be conducting biological weapons research involving the plague, following the mysterious death of a worker at a Siberian laboratory.  

The 28‑year‑old worker died on Oct. 2 after being hospitalized with a severe case of pneumonia.  

Global health officials are seeking more information about the death, prompting the World.
