title: Paris student protests turn violent, police use tear gas and fireworks
content:
Student protests in Paris turned violent, with tear gas and fireworks reported as clashes erupted.  

School pupils demanding better funding confronted riot police, part of a wave of nationwide protests over shortages and crumbling schools. The confrontations in the capital led police to deploy tear gas against the demonstrators.
summary: Clashes erupted in Paris as school pupils demanding better funding faced riot police. The protests are part of nationwide demonstrations over shortages and crumbling schools.
author: Euronews

title: Israelis hold ceremonies at Nova site and Kfar Aza, three years after Hamas attack
content:
Israelis gathered at the Nova festival site and in Kfar Aza to mourn the victims of the October 7 Hamas‑led attack, three years after the assault that ignited the Gaza war.

The ceremonies marked the anniversary of the Hamas‑led October 7 attack, which sparked the ongoing conflict in Gaza.
summary: Ceremonies were held at the Nova festival site and in Kfar Aza. They marked three years since the Hamas‑led October 7 attack that sparked the Gaza war.
author: Euronews

title: Haiti indefinitely postpones December and February elections amid gang violence
content:
Haiti’s electoral council announced on Tuesday that the country’s elections, originally set for December and February, have been postponed indefinitely. The council cited technical and operational requirements, noting that ongoing gang violence continues to disrupt election preparations.

The postponement leaves Haitians without a democratic process as authorities work to register voters and secure the areas needed for a poll. No new date for the elections has been provided.
summary: Haiti’s electoral council said the December and February elections are postponed indefinitely, citing technical and operational requirements. Gang violence continues to disrupt voter registration and security for the polls, leaving the country without a democratic process.
author: France 24

title: Lionel Messi bids farewell, scores in 3-0 win over Benin at Monumental Stadium
content:
Lionel Messi said farewell to Argentina fans Tuesday in an emotional final international appearance.  

He scored in a 3‑0 win over Benin at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium.  

The match was watched by 85,000 supporters who celebrated the end of a career that brought the country its long‑awaited 2022 World Cup triumph.
summary: Lionel Messi said farewell to Argentina fans on Tuesday in his final international appearance, scoring in a 3-0 win over Benin at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium. The match was attended by 85,000 supporters who celebrated the end of a career that delivered Argentina's 2022 World Cup triumph.
author: France 24

title: Israel to hold memorials for third anniversary of Oct. 7 Hamas attack amid election campaign
content:
Israel will observe the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack on Wednesday with memorial events held across the country.  

Heightened security will surround the commemorations as voters prepare for an upcoming election in which the deadliest day in Israel’s history is expected to remain a central issue.
summary: Israel will mark the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack with memorial events across the country on Wednesday. Heightened security will surround the commemorations as voters prepare for an election where the deadliest day in Israel’s history is expected to remain a central issue.
author: France 24

title: Israel commemorates third anniversary of Hamas Oct 7 attacks, all hostages home
content:
Live: Israel marks three years since Hamas’s deadly October 7 attacks

Israelis began commemorations on Wednesday for the victims of Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attacks. The attacks killed 1,200 people and saw 251 hostages taken.

This year – the third anniversary of the attacks – is the first time all the hostages or their remains are home.

Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
summary: Israelis began commemorations on Wednesday for the victims of Hamas's October 7, 2023 attacks that killed 1,200 people and involved 251 hostages. The third anniversary marks the first time all hostages or their remains have been returned home.
author: France 24

title: Netanyahu seeks political survival three years after October 7 attacks
content:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is fighting for political survival as Israel heads to legislative elections later this month, three years after the deadly Hamas‑led attacks on October 7 in southern Israel.  

Reports that Arab leaders warned him of the assault in advance have undercut Netanyahu’s claims that Israel’s security chiefs were to blame.  

Despite the controversy, his political base appears to be holding.
summary: Three years after the deadly Hamas-led October 7 attacks in southern Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is fighting for political survival ahead of legislative elections later this month. Reports that Arab leaders warned him of the assault in advance have undercut his claims that Israel's security chiefs are to blame, but his political base appears to be holding.
author: France 24

title: Lionel Messi scores in Argentina's 3-0 win over Benin in his final match
content:
Lionel Messi scored in Argentina’s 3‑0 victory over Benin, marking his final appearance for the national team.  

The match concluded with a 3‑0 win for Argentina, and a full tribute to Messi was presented both before and after the game.
summary: Lionel Messi scored as Argentina defeated Benin 3-0. The game was his final appearance for Argentina and he received a full tribute before and after the match.
author: France 24

title: At least two killed in Kyiv fire after massive strikes
content:
At least two people were killed in a fire in Kyiv after President Volodymyr Zelensky described the incident as the result of “massive strikes” on the Ukrainian capital on Wednesday.  

Ukraine has faced a surge in attacks in recent weeks, with Russian forces targeting energy infrastructure as well as rail and road transport networks.
summary: At least two people were killed in a fire in Kyiv after President Volodymyr Zelensky described "massive strikes" on the capital on Wednesday. Ukraine has faced increased attacks in recent weeks, with Russian strikes targeting energy infrastructure and rail and road transport.
author: France 24

title: Spain PM Pedro Sanchez calls early election; housing, migration and Vox dominate campaign
content:
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called an early election in Spain, describing the move as a gamble.  

Analysts note that the campaign is expected to focus on three main issues: the country’s housing crisis, migration concerns and the growing influence of the right‑wing populist Vox party.
summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is taking a gamble by calling an early election in Spain. The housing crisis, migration and the rise of the right‑wing populist Vox party are likely to dominate the campaign.
author: DW World

title: Lionel Messi scores and assists in Argentina's 3-0 farewell win
content:
Argentina defeated its opponent 3-0 in what was Lionel Messi’s final match for the national team.  

Messi contributed directly to all three goals, scoring one and creating two additional chances that were converted by teammates.  

The victory served as a farewell to the country’s most decorated footballer.
summary: Messi scored a goal and provided two assists as Argentina defeated their opponent 3-0. The match marked Argentina's farewell to its most decorated footballer.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Yemen's conflict leaves over 137,000 students without school access
content:
Displaced children in Yemen are longing to resume their studies as the country’s education system remains under severe strain.  

According to recent figures, more than 137,000 students in conflict‑affected areas have lost access to schooling, deepening an already dire crisis for Yemen’s education sector.
summary: More than 137,000 students in conflict zones have lost access to education. The loss deepens Yemen's already dire schooling crisis.
author: Al Jazeera

title: At least two killed in Kyiv during Russia's massive strike on Ukraine
content:
At least two people were killed in Kyiv as Russia launched a “massive” attack on Ukraine.  

Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces carried out a massive strike on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions.  

The strike resulted in casualties in the Ukrainian capital.
summary: At least two people were killed in Kyiv. Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces carried out a massive strike on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gaza City port, once fishing and tourism hub, now shown in ruins after genocide
content:
Gaza City’s port, once a bustling hub for fishing and tourism, has been dramatically altered. The change follows the period described as a genocide.  

Al Jazeera journalist Maram Humaid has documented the remaining conditions at the port, showing what is left after the conflict. The footage highlights the stark contrast between the port’s former role and its present state.
summary: Gaza City’s port was a hub for fishing and tourism before the genocide. Al Jazeera’s Maram Humaid shows what’s left.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russia's fuel crisis could open Central Asian market for Iranian oil
content:
Iran’s oil exports have been hampered by a United States blockade, limiting the country’s ability to sell its petroleum abroad.  

Recent disruptions to Russia’s fuel supply, caused by Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, have created a shortage that could open opportunities for Iranian oil in Central Asian markets.  

Analysts note that the Russian crisis may provide a pathway for Iran to increase its presence in the region despite the ongoing U.S. restrictions.
summary: Iran's oil exports have struggled amid a US blockade. A Russian energy crisis caused by Ukrainian attacks could help Iranian oil.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Houthis strike Aden airport runway; Saudi forces shoot down missile near Riyadh
content:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels launched an attack on Aden’s international airport, and Saudi forces reported downing a missile near Riyadh, officials said.

The Yemeni government said one of the missiles struck Aden airport’s runway only minutes before a scheduled flight from Cairo was due to land, disrupting the approach. Saudi forces intercepted a separate missile in the vicinity of Riyadh, preventing it from reaching its target.
summary: Yemeni officials say a missile struck Aden airport's runway shortly before a scheduled Cairo flight was to land. Saudi forces said they downed a missile near Riyadh.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pornhub back in Australia, limited to adult Apple device users
content:
Pornhub, the world’s most popular adult‑content website, has resumed operations in Australia but is now accessible only to adult users on Apple devices.  

The site was taken offline in March after Australian authorities introduced age‑verification requirements that it could not meet. Its limited return means the platform remains unavailable on non‑Apple hardware.
summary: Pornhub has resumed service in Australia but only for adults using Apple devices. The site was taken offline in March after age‑verification laws were introduced.
author: BBC World

title: Former Bishop of Broome jailed for sexually abusing young men
content:
The former Bishop of Broome, a senior Catholic cleric, has been sentenced to jail after being found guilty of sexually abusing young men.  

His case marks him as one of the most senior Catholic officials worldwide to face sex‑abuse charges.
summary: The former Bishop of Broome, an Australian Catholic cleric, was jailed for sexually abusing young men. He is one of the most senior Catholic clerics worldwide to face sex‑abuse charges.
author: BBC World

title: Ex-US spy David Rush admits $200m scam, providing secrets to foreign government
content:
Former U.S. intelligence officer David Rush has admitted to orchestrating a $200 million fraud scheme and to storing gold bars in his home, according to prosecutors.  

Rush also confessed to passing classified information to a foreign government and disclosed the existence of a “clandestine human source,” officials said.
summary: David Rush, a former U.S. spy, admitted he stashed gold bars in his home as part of a $200 million scam. He also confessed to providing secrets to a foreign government and revealed a “clandestine human source,” prosecutors said.
author: BBC World

title: Survivors of Nir Oz kibbutz return three years after Hamas attack
content:
Three years after the Hamas‑led attack on October 7 that devastated the kibbutz Nir Oz, residents are confronting the challenge of rebuilding. The assault killed 47 people and resulted in 76 hostages being taken.

Some survivors have now returned to live in the community as they grapple with how to reconstruct their homes and lives.
summary: The Nir Oz kibbutz was destroyed in the 7 October Hamas-led attacks. Three years later, some survivors have returned to live there after 47 people were killed and 76 were taken hostage.
author: BBC World

title: USMNT faces Canada in international friendly at Allianz Field
content:
The United States men’s national team faces Canada in an international friendly scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET at Allianz Field in Saint Paul. This match follows the USA’s 3-0 victory over Mexico in their previous outing.

Goalkeeper competition has reopened following shaky performances from World Cup incumbents Matt Freese and Chris Brady, while Diego Kochen impressed in his first start against Mexico. Brian Schwake is expected to start, aiming to translate his recent form with Nashville into his second appearance for the national team.

In defense, Auston Trusty is set to play left-back, potentially partnering with Chris Richards, while Alex Freeman may advance further up the right flank. Mathis Albert earned a surprise start over Zavier Gozo due to his dynamism during the training camp, offering a look at a potential future star for the program.
summary: The United States men's national team will play Canada in a friendly match at Allianz Field in Saint Paul. Goalkeeper competition is described as reopened after shaky performances from Matt Freese and Chris Brady, while Diego Kochen shone in his first start against Mexico.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lionel Messi farewell match live – updates and analysis from Argentina v Benin
content:
Lionel Messi’s farewell match against Argentina and Benin is scheduled to kick off at 7pm ET, marking the end of his professional football career. The event has generated significant online discussion, with The Guardian receiving reader feedback via email regarding the historic occasion.

Among the comments shared by The Guardian, reader Paul engaged with a 20-year-old article about Messi, while another reader, “snafuclarke,” posted a critical opinion arguing that Messi is “hugely overrated.” This specific comment claimed that the hype surrounding the player has not matched his on-pitch performances, with the exception of his most recent game.
summary: Farewell match kicks off at 7pm ETMessi has completed footballEmail Pablo your analysis, jokes and moreGuardian reader Paul reached out via email and is apparently deep in the comments section of a 20-year-old Messi article we published here at the Guardian. I can only hope Guardian reader “snafuclarke” has fully recovered from such a scorchingly terrible take:don’t kid yourselves.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pocognoli's Scotland left with questions after inert performance
content: Sebastien Pocognoli faces scrutiny following a lackluster performance by Scotland, which has left the manager still searching for his first home victory. The match highlighted ongoing domestic disharmony within the squad, prompting questions about the team's direction under his leadership.
summary: Sebastien Pocognoli is left with questions to answer following an inert Scotland performance. The result leaves him still searching for his first home win.
author: BBC Sport

title: Midfield options and a fab front four - what we've learned about England
content:
Phil McNulty has assessed the key takeaways for the England national team following the recent international window. His analysis highlights significant developments in the squad, specifically focusing on the return of Trent Alexander-Arnold and the debut of Alex Scott.

The evaluation also examines the team's tactical options, noting a strong midfield configuration and the emergence of a formidable front four. These factors represent the primary lessons England have gained from the latest period of international fixtures.
summary: From Trent Alexander-Arnold's return to Alex Scott's debut, Phil McNulty assesses what England have learned during this international window.
author: BBC Sport

title: Appeals panel reviews block of RFK Jr.'s vaccine panel appointments
content: The Trump administration argued to a federal appeals panel on Tuesday that a lower court made an error by preventing Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. from installing his chosen members on a major vaccine advisory committee. Justice Department attorney Matthew Zorn presented the case to the 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, asserting that the district court judge lacked the legal power to issue the block.
summary: The Trump administration told a federal appeals panel that a lower court erred in blocking Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s appointees from a vaccine advisory panel. Justice Department attorney Matthew Zorn argued that the district court judge lacked the authority to issue the block.
author: The Hill

title: US renews do-not-travel warning for Russia over suspected pneumonic plague
content:
The U.S. State Department has renewed its warning for Americans not to travel to Russia, citing a suspected case of pneumonic plague in Siberia. The announcement was made on Tuesday via a post on the social platform X.

The State Department stated that the U.S. Embassy is aware of press reports regarding the suspected pneumonic plague in the Irkutsk region.
summary: The U.S. State Department is refreshing its call for Americans not to travel to Russia following a suspected case of pneumonic plague in Siberia. The department stated on X that the U.S. Embassy is aware of press reports regarding the suspected outbreak in the Irkutsk region.
author: The Hill

title: Trump: Government to take 40% stake in Sparrows Point submarine shipyard
content:
President Trump announced on Tuesday that the U.S. government will acquire a 40 percent stake in a planned “next generation” submarine shipyard located in Sparrows Point, Maryland. The industrial area, situated in Baltimore County, was the site of a presidential visit on the same day.

Trump stated that American taxpayers would receive this significant ownership share as part of a commitment to ensuring the enduring success of the shipyard.
summary: President Trump stated that American taxpayers will receive a 40 percent stake in the planned shipyard in Sparrows Point, Md. He made the announcement during a Tuesday visit to the unincorporated industrial area in Baltimore County.
author: The Hill

title: US trade deficit tops $100B in August, highest since March 2025
content: The U.S. trade deficit reached a 17-month high in August, surpassing $100 billion for the first time since March 2025. According to data released Tuesday by the Census Bureau and the Bureau of Economic Analysis, U.S. imports of goods and services exceeded the value of exports by $105.6 billion during that month.
summary: The U.S. trade deficit rose to a 17-month high in August, exceeding $100 billion for the first time since March 2025. Imports of goods and services were worth $105.6 billion more than exports, according to data from the Census Bureau and Bureau of Economic Analysis.
author: The Hill

title: Archdiocese of St. Louis sues ICE officials over blocked religious services
content: The Archdiocese of St. Louis has filed a lawsuit against Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials, alleging that a jail visitation policy obstructs religious services. The legal action contends that the policy prevents Catholic detainees from practicing essential aspects of their faith.
summary: The lawsuit argues that the jail's visitation policy prevents Catholic detainees from practicing important parts of their faith.
author: The Hill

title: Planned Parenthood Votes adds $1M to ads targeting Maine, Michigan Senate races
content: Planned Parenthood Votes, a super PAC affiliated with Planned Parenthood, is investing an additional $1 million in ad buys to support Democratic Senate candidates in Maine and Michigan. The funds will be used for digital ad campaigns targeting incumbent Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) and former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.).
summary: Planned Parenthood Votes is investing an additional $1 million in digital ad campaigns to boost Democratic Senate candidates in Maine and Michigan. The funds will target Senator Susan Collins of Maine and former Representative Mike Rogers of Michigan.
author: The Hill

title: Plague in Russia sparks concern, COVID-19 pandemic memories: 5 things to know
content: The death of a Russian laboratory technician researching the plague has raised concerns both domestically and internationally, with observers drawing parallels to conditions that some theorized preceded the COVID-19 pandemic. Reports surfaced last week indicating that a worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East died shortly after being hospitalized.
summary: The death of Russian lab technician researching the plague has set off alarms abroad and at home as observers note resemblances to the conditions that some theorized preceded the COVID-19 pandemic. Reports emerged last week that a laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East had died shortly after being hospitalized.  The news…
author: The Hill

title: Green member behind Zionism motion named as 'close friend' of jailed al-Qaeda supporter in court
content:
Lubna Speitan, a Green Party member who introduced a motion on Zionism, has been identified in court as a "close friend" of Minh Quang Pham. Pham is currently serving a 40-year prison sentence following a Heathrow bomb plot investigation.

Speitan has offered to testify on Pham’s behalf during the legal proceedings.
summary: Lubna Speitan offered to testify on behalf of Minh Quang Pham, who was jailed for 40 years after a Heathrow bomb plot investigation.
author: BBC Politics

title: Hunter Valley group wins landmark high court climate change case over Mount Pleasant coalmine
content:
A Hunter Valley community group has secured a victory in Australia’s first High Court case to address climate change, a ruling advocates describe as a binding national precedent for fossil fuel projects in New South Wales. The nation’s highest court upheld a unanimous decision from the NSW Court of Appeal, which had previously overturned the proposed expansion of MACH Energy’s Mount Pleasant coalmine in Muswellbrook.

The community group stated that the ruling demonstrates that society "cannot continue to dig up coal … and pretend the consequences have nothing to do with us." This landmark judgment effectively blocks the mine expansion, marking a significant legal development regarding the intersection of climate change and industrial development in the region.
summary: A Hunter Valley community group won Australia's first high court case to consider climate change, with the ruling setting a binding national precedent for fossil fuel projects in New South Wales. The nation's highest court upheld a unanimous ruling by the NSW court of appeal that overturned MACH Energy's proposed expansion of its Mount Pleasant coalmine in Muswellbrook.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Study: about one‑third of lupus patients use supplement‑med combos that may interact
content:
A recent study published online on September 22 in Arthritis Care & Research found that nearly one in three patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are taking a supplement‑medication combination that could potentially interact.

The research highlights the prevalence of such combinations among people with SLE, underscoring the importance of monitoring for possible drug‑supplement interactions.
summary: Nearly one in three patients with systemic lupus erythematosus are taking a supplement‑medication combination with potential for an interaction. The result was reported in a study published online Sept. 22 in Arthritis Care & Research.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UK study links pregnancy complications to higher cardiac and renal risk
content: A U.K. study published in the open-access journal BMJ Medicine indicates that women experiencing complications during their latest or previous pregnancies face an elevated risk of developing cardiometabolic-renal conditions in the years following delivery. The research highlights a link between these pregnancy-related health issues and subsequent cardiac and renal health problems.
summary: A UK study published in BMJ Medicine suggests women with pregnancy complications face elevated risks of cardiometabolic-renal conditions. This increased risk applies to complications in either the latest or a previous pregnancy.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Frozen yoghurt chains return to UK with £12 tubs
content: Frozen yoghurt, a popular trend during the 2000s and 2010s, has experienced a resurgence with multiple chains opening across the wider UK. The return of the treat has sparked questions about its sustainability, particularly given that a single tub now costs £12.
summary: Frozen yoghurt has made a comeback with multiple chains opening across the wider UK. The article questions whether the trend will last given the price of £12 per tub.
author: BBC Business

title: INRAE study finds sorghum may boost European yields under climate change
content:
Research conducted by INRAE and AgroParisTech indicates that global warming could positively impact sorghum yields in Europe. The study identifies sorghum as a viable alternative to maize for livestock feed, noting that the crop requires less water and can tolerate higher temperatures.

The researchers utilized simulations based on past climate data and future climate scenarios to explore new strategies for European agriculture. Their findings were published in the journal Earth's Future.
summary: Research by INRAE and AgroParisTech indicates that global warming could positively impact sorghum yields in Europe. The crop is a promising alternative to maize for livestock feed because it requires less water and tolerates higher temperatures.
author: Phys.org
